answer: Every active agent must emit a fresh signal that traces a spiral of timed hash challenges whose radius grows with the current network tide of recent activity. An attacker spawning N sybils is forced to compute N independent spirals, each requiring roughly fifteen serial minutes of CPU to reach the tide’s current radius, so five hundred fakes lock up five hundred cores for the full window or their signals are discarded. An honest agent completes one spiral and reuses the tide for free.
